Issues.Title: Help.ShowPopup uses wrong text color in Dark mode
Issues.Body: ### .NET version .NET 10.0.404 ### Did it work in .NET Framework? Not tested/verified ### Did it work in any of the earlier releases of .NET Core or .NET 5+? Not tested ### Issue description When using `Help.ShowPopup`, the text color is always forced to black. This works when the color mode is Light (`Classic`), but it makes the text unreadable if it's Dark. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Set the theme to Dark by calling `Application.SetColorMode(SystemColorMode.Dark)` before creating the first `Form`. 2. Create a `Form` with a help button by setting `MinimizeBox` and `MaximizeBox` to `false`, and `HelpButton` to `true`. 3. Inside the `HelpButtonClicked` event handler, call `Help.ShowPopup`. Issues.Title: Initialize ListViewDesigner action lists atomically
Issues.Body:
## Proposed changes

Use a per-designer lock to initialize and publish the action list collection. Build the collection before caching it so concurrent readers share one complete collection and a failed first access leaves initialization retryable.

The concurrent test starts two independent readers together and checks both the contents and the shared reference. A separate test covers an access before Initialize followed by a successful retry.

## Customer Impact

Concurrent first reads consistently return the same collection with the expected ListView action list.

## Regression?

The existing concurrency test failed with two different collection references in [Azure x64 Debug](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_apis/test/Runs/47535556/results/105003?api-version=7.1). The initialization pattern predates that run.

## Risk

The lock is scoped to one ListViewDesigner instance and protects the lazy cache.

## Test methodology

The new early-access test reproduced the empty cache on the baseline in all three configurations. The baseline concurrency test passed 30 repeated runs on these workers. With the exact fix commit, all 13 ListViewDesignerTests passed in 30 x64 Debug rounds, 20 x64 Release rounds, and 20 x86 Debug rounds. Total 910 passed, zero failures, skips, or retries. Builds reported zero warnings and errors. [Windows validation](https://github.com/XFEstudio/winforms/actions/runs/45996129532).

## Test environment(s)

Windows Server 2025, x64 and x86, with the repository .NET 12 SDK. Developed with AI assistance and independently reviewed by an AI agent.

Issues.Title: Stabilize the Windows Forms window snap tests
Issues.Body:
Fixes #15112

## Proposed changes

Verify that the test form is in the foreground before sending the real Win+Left or Win+Right shortcut. Check how many keyboard events Windows accepted, and release any keys that a partial send could leave down. Replace the fixed sleeps and mid-snap Escape with a bounded wait for the original window geometry assertions. Retain all four combinations of direction and initial window state.

## Customer Impact

Reduces intermittent failures in the Windows Forms UI integration tests. The change is limited to FormTests.cs.

## Regression?

The intermittent failure is documented in #15112 and was observed in [upstream build 1702037](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1702037).

## Risk

The tests still exercise Windows Shell snapping. Foreground, input insertion, and bounds failures now report which step failed.

## Test methodology

On interactive Windows workers, all four cases passed on the first attempt in 25 x86 Debug rounds, 25 x86 Release rounds, and 15 x64 Debug rounds. That is 260 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped, with automatic retries disabled for the measurement. The exact commit also passed all five FormTests in each configuration with the repository retry settings. Builds reported zero warnings and errors. The baseline passed all 120 repetitions on these workers, so this run did not reproduce the historical transient. [Windows validation](https://github.com/XFEstudio/winforms/actions/runs/45953282583).

## Test environment(s)

Interactive Windows build 26100 with a same-session Explorer shell, x86 and x64, and the repository .NET 12 SDK. Developed with AI assistance and independently reviewed by an AI agent.

Issues.Title: Fix Issue 12866: TabControl doesn't send the name of selected tab to accessibility clients on initial focus
Issues.Body:
<!-- Please read CONTRIBUTING.md before submitting a pull request -->

Fixes #12866


## Proposed changes

- Updated `TabControlAccessibleObject` to return the correct focused accessibility provider by using native `TCM_GETCURFOCUS`.
- Added focus handling to correctly distinguish between the focused tab and the selected tab when they differ.
- Kept `UIA_HasKeyboardFocusPropertyId` consistent with the object returned by `GetFocus()`.

<!-- We are in TELL-MODE the following section must be completed -->

## Customer Impact

- Fixes an accessibility issue where Narrator announced only "tab control" when a `TabControl` initially received focus instead of announcing the focused tab name.
- Ensures the UIA focus provider correctly represents the focused tab item, improving screen reader behavior and accessibility compliance.

## Regression? 

- Yes

## Risk

- Low. The change is isolated to `TabControlAccessibleObject` focus reporting logic and does not modify the native focus behavior of `TabControl`. Added accessibility tests cover focused, selected, created, uncreated, and empty control scenarios.

<!-- end TELL-MODE -->

### After

When Narrator is running and focus moves to a `TabControl`, it correctly announces the focused tab item (for example, "Tab 1" or "Tab 2") because the accessibility provider returns the appropriate focused tab accessibility object.

- Added validation that an empty focused `TabControl` reports itself as the focused accessibility object.
- Added tests verifying that uncreated controls return `null` without creating handles and that created but unfocused controls also return `null`.
- Added tests to verify that `UIA_HasKeyboardFocusPropertyId` remains consistent with the object returned from `GetFocus()`.
- Validated correct accessibility focus reporting when the `TabControl` receives focus while Narrator is running.
